messages.subject: RenderUI not updating?
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I am having some trouble with RenderUI not updating. Code looks something like this:

#ui.R
shinyUI(fluidPage(
...
 uiOutput("selectUI"),
...


#server.R
gene_info <<- NULL
autocomplete_list <<- NULL

shinyServer(function(input, output){
        observe({
           gene_info <<- read.delim(paste(input$select, '/genes_chngdup.tsv', sep=''), stringsAsFactors=FALSE, sep="\t", header = FALSE)
           autocomplete_list <<- gene_info[,2]

        })

        output$selectUI <- renderUI({
                #print("why doesn't autocomplete_list update")
                textInput.typeahead(
                        id="search",
                       placeholder="eg. TMSB4X",
                        local=data.frame(name=c(autocomplete_list),
                        valueKey = "name",
                        tokens=c(1:length(autocomplete_list),
                        template = HTML("<p class='repo-language'>{{info}}</p> <p class='repo-name'>{{name}}</p>")
                )
        })
}



I was looking at some other resources and some were saying that this is lack of update is intended in certain cases where renderUI keeps getting the same input so it doesn't bother updating -- but when gene_info changes when input$select changes, it doesn't look like renderUI is called again ever. Does anyone know how to get around this? Thanks.

Daniel

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: RenderUI not updating?
parts:
gene_info and autocomplete_list are regular variables--Shiny can't detect changes in them. You could theoretically call makeReactiveBinding for each of them to magically make them reactive values (or make them into members of a reactiveValues object).

But in this case, that's not what you want to do. Instead, change each one of the to a reactive(...) expression--you don't need observe(...) at all here. Check out the shiny reactive programming tutorial videos from the Shiny Developer Conference if you haven't already--this advice should make a lot more sense after that.
